name: Red clover
grown_as: A native short-lived perennial of meadows and grassland, also sown as green manure
habit: Upright to sprawling, 20 to 60 cm, several hairy stems from a crown. Does not root along its stems.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate up the stem, plus long-stalked leaves from the base
leaf.leaflets: All three almost stalkless and alike
leaf.outline: Each leaflet oval to elliptic, 1.5 to 3 cm, longer than wide
leaf.tip: Rounded or bluntly pointed, not notched
leaf.margin: Entire or with very faint teeth
leaf.surface: Softly hairy, especially beneath; usually a pale whitish crescent mark on each leaflet
leaf.stalk: Base leaves long-stalked, upper ones short; triangular stipules with a long bristle tip, pale with purple-red veins
leaf.colour: Mid green with a pale crescent

flower.form: A round to egg-shaped head of many tubular pea flowers
flower.petals: Each flower narrow, a long tube with a small standard
flower.behind: Hairy calyces; the head sits directly on a pair of leaves, cupped by them
flower.carried: Heads at the stem tips with no stalk, set on top of the last pair of leaves

fruit: Tiny pods in the brown dry head; small kidney-shaped seeds, yellow to purple-brown
seedling: Two small oval seed leaves, then a single round first leaf, then hairy three-leaflet leaves
winter: A low rosette of hairy three-leaflet leaves at the base

leaf: three oval leaflets longer than wide
a pale crescent mark on each
bloom: a round pink-purple head of many tubular flowers
the head sitting on a pair of leaves with no stalk
young: three oval leaflets with pale crescents
flower: pink-purple round heads at the stem tips
each head sitting on a pair of leaves, no stalk
seedhead: dry brown heads at the stem tips
dormant: a low rosette of hairy three-leaflet leaves

look_alikes: Zigzag clover (Trifolium medium) has narrower leaflets, zigzag stems and a short stalk under the head. White clover creeps and roots, with white heads on long stalks. Hare's-foot clover has soft grey fluffy heads.
